title: Akama and the Black Temple
summary: Akama hides a plan for the Broken beneath a show of service to Illidan. A trail from Baa’ri to the Black Temple follows his choices, the cost of secrecy, and the recovery of his soul.
opening: Karabor’s darkened temple rules the height above Shadowmoon. Beneath its walls, Akama’s people keep a secret the Betrayer must not discover.

chapters.title: The temple and the hidden plan
chapters.body:
Before a black name crowned the height, Karabor was the draenei’s sacred temple in Shadowmoon Valley. War and occupation stripped that name from its halls; the fortress became the Black Temple. Illidan seized it from Magtheridon, and the Broken under Akama joined his ranks. Their public allegiance did not reveal Akama’s private purpose. Beneath that service endured the memory of what his people had lost.

Among Baa’ri’s ruins, scattered tablets opened a trail toward Akama. Those who sought him came from different camps, yet the valley’s buried history drew their attention to the same hidden purpose. Written orders and fragments of an old medallion lay ahead. Karabor’s name had survived the taking of its halls; now its remnants offered a way to the Broken who still remembered them.

From the ruins, Oronu’s written orders and the Ashtongue shamans drew the seeker deeper into Shadowmoon. Pieces of the Medallion of Karabor were recovered along the way. An apparent servant of Illidan had left instructions in trusted hands. Each clue brought the hidden leader nearer, while the temple whose name the medallion bore remained beneath another master’s shadow.

At the Warden’s Cage, a submerged pool concealed a chamber beyond the outpost. There the seeker found Akama, no longer merely a name in another commander’s orders. The search had reached the leader of the Broken. Yet his place beside Illidan still hid what he meant to do, and the quiet of the chamber offered little assurance of the dangers beyond it.

Akama demanded proof of loyalty, sending the seeker against Ashtongue who threatened his concealment. His Deathsworn remained the trusted circle, while his outward service to Illidan continued. Secrecy had become a harsh burden. To preserve the chance of freedom, the hidden leader maintained an allegiance that concealed his purpose from the master he intended to oppose.

Illidan’s rule made open revolt a danger to the Broken, so Akama’s plan grew in secret. Maiev Shadowsong was imprisoned in his hidden quarters, her own anger at Illidan undiminished. Their purposes drew them toward the same enemy without making them easy allies. Beneath the Warden’s Cage, the hope of escape rested beside the uncertain promise of vengeance.

chapters.title: The seer’s warning
chapters.body:
The search led to the Arcatraz, a crystalline prison suspended above Netherstorm. There the seeker found Seer Udalo already dead. A keeper of the Ashtongue secret had fallen far from Shadowmoon. Akama received the news, and the living were left to follow what little the seer had managed to leave behind. The prison yielded a loss before it yielded a way onward.

Udalo had left a single word upon the floor: Ata’mal. Akama understood it as a place to seek. From the silent prison, that slender clue led back toward the valley’s old temple terraces. The seer could offer no further counsel, yet the name endured him. What waited beneath it remained unknown until the seeker reached the height.

At Ata’mal Terrace, the seeker recovered the Heart of Fury. Akama recognized it from Velen’s past and weighed its power against his people’s freedom. He would not free the Broken only to take Illidan’s place as their master. He sent the artifact onward to A’dal. In that refusal, the hidden struggle found its clearest purpose: freedom rather than another lord.

Akama placed the Heart within the Medallion of Karabor and sent it to A’dal in Shattrath. He promised to stand with the seeker against Illidan. The medallion carried the sacred temple’s name into a dangerous alliance, joining an old inheritance to the hope of liberation. The harder struggle still waited inside the Black Temple, where Akama remained bound to the power he opposed.

chapters.title: A secret under pressure
chapters.body:
In Serpentshrine Cavern, Seer Olum brought fearful news. Vashj’s followers had uncovered the Deathsworn’s secret and tortured him for it. He had kept silent, but the plan was endangered. The burden of concealment had fallen upon another of Akama’s companions. Now the hidden leader had to face what that silence had cost, and what his friend could still endure.

At the Warden’s Cage, Olum chose the spirit world rather than risk giving his captors the secret. Akama helped him die among his brothers. To divert Illidan’s suspicion, Akama then revealed a genuine betrayal by Kael’thas. Olum’s sacrifice left no triumph in its wake. It preserved the hidden purpose at the cost of one of its oldest companions.

In Tempest Keep, the seeker wore an Ashtongue Cowl and killed Al’ar, Kael’thas’s phoenix, under the appearance of obeying Illidan. Akama needed the outward allegiance to seem faithful again. Beneath the borrowed guise, the conspiracy endured. The Ashtongue had yet to rise openly; their hope still depended upon a master believing that those who served him remained his own.

Akama sought the Time-Phased Phylactery once held by Rage Winterchill. Through the Caverns of Time, the adventurer entered a memory of the Battle of Mount Hyjal and recovered it. The struggle of an earlier age yielded an object needed in the present. From that remembered battlefield, the phylactery returned to Shadowmoon, where Akama hoped its power could answer a captivity hidden within his own being.

The phylactery’s power over souls made Akama’s design plain. His own soul was imprisoned in the Black Temple, apart from the leader his people saw. He intended to reclaim it before facing Illidan. The long deception now bore a personal wound as well as a people’s hope. Whether the artifact would suffice remained to be learned within the fortress itself.

chapters.title: Inside the Black Temple
chapters.body:
Xi’ri and the Sha’tar drew Illidan’s defenders outward while Akama, Maiev and the Deathsworn moved upon the fortress. Maiev pursued her own vengeance when she broke from the plan, and Akama continued with his people. At the southern wall, an opening admitted them. The temple that had once sheltered the draenei now received those who came to challenge its ruler.

Inside the Black Temple, the seeker found Akama’s Deathsworn and Seer Kanai. Their message was simple: Akama needed help. The concealed plan had become a confrontation within Illidan’s fortress. The Ashtongue remained beneath his influence, and their leader’s soul was still bound. Before they could turn together against the Betrayer, that hold had to be broken.

With help from the adventurers, Akama defeated his Shade and reclaimed the soul held apart from him. The Ashtongue turned from Illidan’s sway. The blow against the Betrayer began among his own servants before it reached the summit. For a people already brought close to ruin, open resistance had seemed too dangerous. Now their leader stood whole, and the hidden hope became revolt.

After the Council fell, the spirits of Udalo and Olum opened the way to Illidan’s sanctum. One had left the word that led Akama toward Ata’mal; the other had given his life to guard the secret. Now both seers acted beyond death. Their long fidelity brought the company to the last door, where the purpose they had preserved awaited its reckoning.

At last, Akama and the adventurers faced Illidan atop the Black Temple. The Betrayer fell. From Baa’ri’s ruined tablets to the fortress summit, the search had become a struggle for freedom. Akama had reclaimed his soul, and the Ashtongue had risen from Illidan’s control. Karabor’s future remained unwritten, but the shadow of its ruler no longer held them as before.

reviewNote: Complete illustrated twenty-scene research story with original environmental scenes and distinct story figures/objects, source and claim links for every node, accessible transcript playback, and generated voice-over. Original TBC quest/build capture and a human comparison against the matching 2.4.3 client/model remain open; all records stay at research status. The Aldor and Scryer openings and Hyjal raid access are explicit alternatives/mechanics, not events that every adventurer personally combined. The Hyjal scene is labeled a historical time instance. The story ends with Illidan’s TBC defeat and makes no claim that Karabor was immediately restored or imports later Legion/Cataclysm outcomes.
